name: House of Cards
description: House of Cards is a dual-purpose term. While it commonly refers to the physical act of building towers with playing cards, it is also a specific, traditional drawing and building game. In its game form, players compete to build virtual 'rooms' and 'stories' by matching colors and ranks to score points based on triangle formations.

overview.description: House of Cards is a dual-purpose term. While it commonly refers to the physical act of building towers with playing cards, it is also a specific, traditional drawing and building game. In its game form, players compete to build virtual 'rooms' and 'stories' by matching colors and ranks to score points based on triangle formations.

history.origins: Derived from architectural parlor games of the 18th century, where cards were used as visual aids or components for geometric challenges.
timeline: 1700s: Use of cards for building physical structures becomes a popular parlor trick.
19th Century: Rule-based games emerge using building as a metaphor for scoring.
Present: Primary meaning shifted to physical building, but 'scoring' variants survive in game collections.
history.cultural: Symbolizes the fragility of systems; has become a powerful political and social metaphor.
history.evolution: The game evolved from a purely physical challenge into a 'card placement' game where the structure is built mathematically/virtually on a score sheet.

setup.players: Two players. Each player is assigned a color (Red or Black) in the common half-deck variant; with the full deck both take turns placing cards to build the shared house structure.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Often split by color (Red vs Black).
setup.dealing: Players draw cards to their hand (usually 3 at a time) to build their 'house'.

rules.objective: Score the most points by forming specific geometric patterns (triangles) using your assigned color.
rules.gameplay:
1. Players take turns placing cards on the table to 'build' a house.
2. **Valleys**: Two cards placed side-by-side on the base.
3. **Floors**: A horizontal card placed over a 'valley'.
4. **Peaks (Triangles)**: Two cards leaning against each other over a floor.
5. Points are awarded when a triangle is closed. If the majority of cards in a specific 'story' or triangle are of your color, you score the face value of those cards.
keyRules: Build from base: valleys (two cards side-by-side), then floors (horizontal over a valley), then peaks (two cards leaning over a floor).
When a triangle is closed, the player whose color holds the majority in that story scores the face value of those cards.
Players take turns placing one card at a time to extend the structure.

strategy.basic: Prioritize placing your color on the 'high-value' peaks. Save your Aces and Face cards for a peak that covers multiple stories.
strategy.intermediate: Blocking: Use your opponent's color to complete a base so you don't have to waste your own cards on the low-value foundation.
strategy.advanced: Tactical collapse: In some variants, you can force a 'collapse' if you can't win, triggering a penalty for the opponent if they were the last to place a card.
tips: Think of the game as a tiered competition; higher floors yield more points.
Balance your hand between foundation cards (number cards) and scoring cards (face cards).
